findings.evidence: The proof splits a two-variable Riemann integral over [0,T]^2 into triangle-slice integrals and uses slice lengths T-u, but its declared dependencies provide only the C*-algebra definition and one-variable norm-Riemann integration. Neither establishes product-region Fubini or change of integration order. The assigned consumer reaches this item through thm-qsm-dt-variance-green-kubo. Add an exact product-region Fubini prerequisite and prove triangular-cutoff integrability, or supply the slice calculation locally. The identity is true and the gap is locally closable.

The locator describes MIT Lecture 3 equations (3.1)–(3.8) as stationary current correlations. The cited PDF instead derives mean-square displacement from a fluid-particle velocity autocorrelation, including its stationarity relation (3.3); it does not describe a lattice charge-current correlation. The source can remain as a classical correlation analogy with an accurate locator.

After applying FTC II to (tF(t))'=F(t)+tC(t), the proof isolates integral_0^T F(t)dt and rewrites it as integral_0^T (T-u)C(u)du. This uses linearity/additivity of the real Riemann integral, which is not named at that transition in Facts F4–F7. Cite the exact linearity result or show the Riemann-sum rearrangement; the omission is immediately closable.

The supplier definition assigns charge unit Q to q_j, but the witness sets q_j=|j><j| with no charge scale or declared normalization. The resulting J_3 and c=omega(J_3^2) have units 1/s and 1/s^2, not Q/s and Q^2/s^2. Scale each projection by a fixed charge unit and carry its square into c, or state the adopted normalized charge convention; as written the witness does not meet the definition's unit hypotheses.
